q: Who does the statue in the middle of Place des Palmistes depict?
x: Félix Éboué, born in Cayenne, governor and a leading figure of Free France. The monument dates from 1957.

q: Where does the name of Fort Cépérou come from?
x: Cépérou was a Kali'na chief who ceded the hill to the French around 1643.

q: Which soup is the institution of Cayenne market?
x: Under the market hall, phở counters run by Hmong families serve it from breakfast time.

q: In which year was Cayenne's market hall inaugurated?
x: Decided in 1907, the hall was inaugurated in 1910.

q: Which convict painted the penal colony scenes shown at the Franconie museum?
x: Francis Lagrange painted penal colony life. Pierre Huguet is the painter credited with Iracoubo church.

q: Who founded the Loyola estate in 1668?
x: The Jesuits made it a large estate of over 1,000 hectares, with about 500 enslaved people at its peak.

q: Why is the sea brown at Montjoly?
x: The current carries sediment from the Amazon along the coast.

q: Why don't people swim in the Rorota lakes?
x: The trail runs along the Rorota, Lalouette and Rémire lakes, which supply the area with drinking water.

q: How high is the summit of Mont Grand Matoury?
x: 254 m. Mont Bourda rises to about 114 m.

q: In which year did the first rocket lift off from Kourou?
x: On 9 April 1968, with the Véronique sounding rocket.

q: On which of the Salvation Islands is landing forbidden?
x: Visitors go to Île Royale and Île Saint-Joseph. Devil's Island, where political deportees were held, is closed to landings.

q: Who has owned the Salvation Islands since 1971?
x: The French space agency (CNES); the islands also serve as a launch viewing post.

q: Which prisoner was held on Devil's Island from 1895 to 1899?
x: Captain Dreyfus, wrongly convicted, spent more than four years there.

q: What was the Dreyfus tower in Kourou?
o: A signal station linked to the Salvation Islands
x: Inaugurated in 1856, it relayed signals between the Kourou penitentiary and the islands.

q: Who were the 'Annamites' of the Montagne des Singes penal camp?
x: Political and common-law prisoners from Indochina, sent to French Guiana from 1931.

q: To whom does tradition attribute the paintings in Iracoubo church?
x: Pierre Huguet is said to have painted about 600 m² between 1891 and 1893.

q: How many convicts passed through the Transportation Camp?
x: More than 50,000. About 17,000 is the number of relégués.

q: Who did the 1885 relegation law send to French Guiana?
x: Repeat offenders, often petty criminals, interned in the colony for life.

q: Which country does the Maroni form a border with?
x: The Maroni separates French Guiana from Suriname; the Oyapock separates it from Brazil.

q: How many pirogues cross the Maroni each day, by estimates?
x: More than 1,000 crossings a day, including hundreds of children going to school.

q: Who founded Mana in 1828?
x: Mother Anne-Marie Javouhey, founder of the Sisters of Saint Joseph of Cluny.

q: By how much have leatherback turtles declined on Les Hattes beach?
x: According to Kwata. A hatchery has protected the nests since 2023.

q: How high are the Voltaire Falls?
x: About 35 m, among the highest in French Guiana.

q: In which year did the first Hmong refugees arrive in Cacao?
x: In September 1977, about 500 people.

q: Which country had the Hmong refugees of Cacao fled?
x: Laos, via Thailand, after the communist takeover.

q: How long is the Molokoï trail?
x: About 18 km between Cacao and the Coralie track, with shelters halfway.

q: Which animal of the Kaw marshes is South America's largest crocodilian?
x: Kaw shelters one of the last stable populations of black caiman.

q: How big is the Kaw-Roura marshes reserve?
x: About 94,700 ha. 2,464 ha is the Trésor reserve.

q: What colour is the male cock-of-the-rock?
x: Bright orange, with a fan-shaped crest. Females are browner.

q: Which town does the Oyapock bridge link to Saint-Georges?
x: Oiapoque, in Brazil. Albina faces Saint-Laurent, in Suriname.

q: In which year did the Oyapock bridge open to traffic?
x: Finished in 2011, it only opened on 20 March 2017.

q: What is an inselberg?
o: A rock dome rising from the forest
x: The German word means 'island mountain'. Roche Virginie is a granite dome.

q: In French Guiana, what is a pripri?
x: A freshwater marsh of the coastal plain, like the Yiyi pripris at Sinnamary.

q: How do you get to the village of Saül?
x: No road leads to Saül, in the centre of French Guiana.

q: What record does Maripasoula hold?
o: Most populous commune in French Guiana
x: About 18,360 km², slightly more than Kuwait.

q: Which university is linked to the creation of the Trésor reserve?
x: The Trésor foundation, linked to Utrecht University, bought the land.

q: What was the Vidal estate?
o: A sugar plantation worked by enslaved people
x: Established in the early 19th century, abandoned around 1880.

q: What was the old name of Place des Palmistes?
x: Long called 'la Savane', then Place de l'Esplanade, it was laid out from 1821.

q: Where do the royal palms of Place des Palmistes come from?
x: They are Roystonea oleacea; replanting explains the different heights.

q: Where is Félix Éboué buried?
x: Born in Cayenne, governor and Free France figure, he rests in the Panthéon; his statue has stood on the square since 1957.

q: What has the Thémire house held since 1908?
x: It is one of the finest Creole houses on the square.

q: In which year did Poncet de Brétigny acquire Cépérou hill?
x: A first wooden fort was built there: the birth of Cayenne.

q: Which Dutch admiral forced the fort to surrender in 1676?
x: He landed 900 men near the fort.

q: How high above the sea is the top of Fort Cépérou?
x: High enough to take in the town, the estuary and the ocean.

q: Which days is Cayenne market held?
x: Saturday is the busiest day: come early.

q: On which square is Cayenne market held?
x: Esplanade and Savane are former names of Place des Palmistes.

q: In which year was the Museum of Guianese Cultures founded?
x: 1901 is when the Franconie museum opened.

q: Roughly how many objects does the Museum of Guianese Cultures hold?
x: Plus archaeology collections, images and sound archives.

q: In which year did the Franconie museum open?
x: It is one of French Guiana's oldest cultural institutions.

q: How many specimens are in Father Barbotin's insect collection?
x: It is part of the Franconie museum's cabinet of curiosities.

q: How big can a leatherback turtle get?
x: A giant: it nests on the beaches of Rémire-Montjoly.

q: Besides the leatherback, which turtle mostly nests at Montjoly?
x: More rarely, the green and hawksbill turtles.

q: When do turtles nest at Montjoly?
x: Hatchlings keep emerging afterwards.

q: Who owns the Montjoly Salines site?
x: First plots acquired in 1981; the Kwata association has managed it since 2012.

q: What does the boardwalk at the Salines cross?
x: One of the few mangroves in French Guiana you can reach on foot.

q: How long is the Rorota loop?
x: About 150 m of ascent, 1 h 30 to 2 h.

q: Which mountain is the Rorota trail on?
x: It links up with the Topu and Loyola trails on the same massif.

q: Which Loyola ruin can be seen from the Rémire road?
x: The windmill is a historic monument; the ruins have been listed since 1993.

q: Which university has excavated at Loyola?
x: The site has been excavated since the 1990s.

q: Why was the Loyola estate abandoned after 1763?
o: The Society of Jesus was banned
A road was built through it
x: The Jesuits had already given up sugar around 1740.

q: At the mouth of which river is Fort Diamant?
x: It guarded the entrance to the island of Cayenne.

q: How thick are the walls of Fort Diamant?
x: Basalt and brick; a grassy bank was meant to hide it from ships.

q: What stands at the top of Mont Bourda?
x: Vegetation has partly closed the view, but the sea shows along the way.

q: What record does the Mont Grand Matoury reserve hold?
o: Largest peri-urban nature reserve in France
x: About 2,123 ha of rainforest in the heart of Cayenne island.

q: In which year was the Mont Grand Matoury reserve created?
x: By decree of 6 September 2006. 1998 is the Kaw reserve.

q: Behind which institution does the Montabo hill trail start?
x: On the Montabo road; about 3.8 km, marked.

q: What is the other name of the Vidal estate?
x: Saint-Régis is where the Jesuits moved their sugar works; Thémire is a house in Cayenne.

q: Which birds can you see on the way to the Vidal estate?
x: The secondary forest is rich in birds: black-necked aracaris, channel-billed toucans, hermits.

q: Who manages the Montagne Topu trail?
x: A marked 3.3 km loop on the heights of Mahury.

q: Who announced the space centre in French Guiana in 1964?
x: On 21 March 1964, in Cayenne.

q: Why was Kourou chosen for the space centre?
x: Also: few hurricanes or earthquakes, and a low population density.

q: In which year did Ariane 1 first lift off?
x: On 24 December 1979. 1968 was the Véronique sounding rocket.

q: How large is the Guiana Space Centre?
x: It is Europe's spaceport.

q: Which launchers does the space centre tour show?
x: The guided bus tour is free on booking, with ID.

q: How old are the rocks of Pointe des Roches in Kourou?
x: Granodiorites crossed by pegmatite veins.

q: What role did Île Saint-Joseph have in the penal colony?
o: Solitary confinement, in silence and darkness
x: Political deportees went to Devil's Island, convicts to Île Royale.

q: How many visitors did the Salvation Islands receive in 2017?
x: It is French Guiana's top tourist site.

q: What is the origin of the Salvation Islands?
x: Three volcanic islands about fifteen kilometres off Kourou.

q: How did the Guiana zoo start in 1983?
x: It became a zoo in 1985, closed in 2007 and reopened in 2008.

q: Who took over the Guiana zoo for its 2008 reopening?
o: The creators of the Balata garden in Martinique
x: It houses over 450 animals of Guianese and Amazonian wildlife.

q: Which commune is the Annamites penal camp in?
x: The Crique Anguille camp; about 5 km out and back from the road.

q: Until when did the Crique Anguille camp operate?
x: From 1931 to 6 December 1944; mortality was high.

q: How large is the Grand Pripri de Yiyi?
x: Marshes, mangroves and flooded savannahs between the Sinnamary and Iracoubo rivers.

q: Which association, French Guiana's oldest nature group, co-manages Yiyi?
x: With the commune of Sinnamary, for the Coastal Conservancy.

q: What nickname is sometimes given to Iracoubo church?
x: For its 600 m² of colourful naive paintings.

q: What did Pierre Huguet do a few weeks after the church was consecrated?
x: The church was consecrated on 6 January 1893; Huguet escaped on 20 February.

q: What does the memorial outside Iracoubo commemorate?
o: Kali'na and Arawak people exhibited in 'human zoos'
x: 47 people taken to Europe in 1882 and 1892.

q: How high is the Montagne des Singes?
x: At the top, an ONF shelter overlooks the canopy and the space centre.

q: Which butterfly do you often see at Montagne des Singes?
x: The monkeys, despite the name, are rare.

q: How many lakes does Kourou have?
x: Bois Diable, Marie-Claire and Bois Chaudat.

q: In which year was Saint-Laurent-du-Maroni officially inaugurated?
x: On 21 January 1858, after the penal colony moved west.

q: Which famous convict is a cell at the Transportation Camp attributed to?
x: Jean Valjean and Edmond Dantès are novel characters.

q: Since when has Saint-Laurent-du-Maroni been a Town of Art and History?
x: Its heritage centre occupies several blocks of the camp.

q: Where did the first relégués arrive in 1887?
x: On 20 June 1887; nothing was ready and they built their own camp.

q: In which year was the border fixed on the Maroni's median line?
x: It is France's fifth-longest land border.

q: Which Surinamese town faces Saint-Laurent?
x: An official ferry links the two banks.

q: In which year was the Hmong village of Javouhey founded?
x: A year after Cacao; 1828 is when Mana was founded.

q: What task did the government give Anne-Marie Javouhey at Mana?
o: Preparing hundreds of enslaved people for freedom
x: The Mana colony was then independent of Cayenne.

q: In which year was Anne-Marie Javouhey beatified?
x: She had left French Guiana in 1843.

q: Which commune is Les Hattes beach in?
x: On Kali'na land, about twenty kilometres from Mana.

q: What is the natural hatchery on Les Hattes beach called?
x: Run since 2023 by the Kwata association with the Amana reserve and customary chiefs.

q: In which year was the Amana nature reserve created?
x: To protect one of the world's largest leatherback nesting sites.

q: Which track leads to the Voltaire Falls?
x: About 70 km of laterite from Saint-Laurent. The Coralie track leads to the Molokoï.

q: How many days does the Hmong New Year last in Cacao?
x: It takes place in December.

q: Which museum is in Cacao?
o: Le Planeur Bleu, with thousands of insects
x: The other three are in Cayenne and Kourou.

q: How long does the full Molokoï crossing take?
x: Most hikers split it over two days, with a night in a shelter.

q: Which river is the village of Roura on?
x: It is the gateway to the East, at the start of the Kaw road.

q: Which botanist was behind the Trésor reserve?
x: A Dutch botanist living in French Guiana, he started the land purchase.

q: Which bird has its largest known breeding colony at Kaw?
x: The marshes also host hoatzins, scarlet ibis and cocoi herons.

q: How far is the Kaw landing from Roura?
x: Via departmental road 6; the village is then reached by pirogue.

q: Where does the cock-of-the-rock build its nest?
o: At the top of tall trees
x: Hence its name. A nesting site lies along the Kaw road.

q: In which year was Saint-Georges linked to Cayenne by road?
x: 2017 is when the bridge to Brazil opened.

q: How tall are the pylons of the Oyapock bridge?
x: A 378 m cable-stayed bridge.

q: Which Amerindian people has about 500 members in Saint-Georges?
x: The town also has a strong French-Brazilian feel.

q: How high is the top of Roche Virginie?
x: High enough to look out over the canopy.

q: Which plants grow on the Roche Virginie slab?
x: A rare rock-savannah vegetation, listed as a natural area of interest.

q: Which river is Saut Maripa on?
x: About twenty kilometres south-west of Saint-Georges.

q: How many people did Saül and its settlements have during the gold rushes?
x: About a hundred people live there today.

q: In which year was the Amazonian Park of French Guiana created?
x: On 27 February 2007: the largest national park in France and the EU.

q: Which country claims about a tenth of Maripasoula's territory?
x: The commune lies on the upper Maroni, facing Suriname.

q: What do you need to visit the Amerindian villages south of Élahé?
x: They are in a restricted-access zone.

q: Which road are the Fourgassié falls on?
x: A few kilometres from Roura, in primary forest.

q: Which of these products is sold at Saint-Laurent market?
x: Along with fruit, vegetables, spices and Maroni cooking.
